families.description: Optical module replaced on an older transmission node: link up, traffic counters zero; interface reset restores forwarding. Outcome reported once and retold twice.
Remote radio site resets from unstable DC power; rectifier swap helps briefly, then it recurs and a loose breaker terminal is found. Site access instructions live only in an email.
BGP sessions flap after a firmware upgrade on aggregation routers. One case is a changed hold-timer default fixed by config rollback; a lookalike on another router is a link with CRC errors.

High inlet temperature in an outdoor cabinet: a clogged dust filter fixes it briefly, then it returns and a stalling fan tray is found. Two NOC staff report the second alarm separately. Later guidance qualifies the earlier advice.

A config template push breaks the voice VLAN on access switches. Rolling back works on the old model; on a newer model it fails, and that lesson sits in a private change-review channel the junior NOC engineer cannot see.
Intermittent CRC errors on a hub uplink. SFP swap does not help; days later the patch cord is found pinched by the cabinet door. The one person who fitted the permanent fix is on leave.

A microwave hop site on weak mains drops in the evenings. A PSU swap helps for three weeks, then the drops return; the real cause is voltage sag and an aged battery string. Winter access instructions exist only in an email.

BGP and port flaps after a firmware upgrade depend on the line card revision. LC-2 is fixed by a patch (reported twice by different people, then retold in an email); LC-3 needs a vendor workaround recorded only in a private core channel.

Optical module replaced on a transport node: local link up, far-end loss of signal. A line card power cycle is advised but the outcome is never reported. A colleague mentioned as an expert only handled an older equipment family.

A rooftop cabinet raises a high temperature alarm that is really a lowered alarm threshold from a firmware config bundle. Fixed remotely and confirmed the next day. Roof access instructions live in an email; the engineer who knows the bundle rollout is on leave.
